When writing, avoid unclear or illogical comparisons.

header.text: An unclear comparison occurs when a comparison has more than one possible interpretation.

text.text: Marco is more annoyed by the noise than his sister.

header.text: There are two possible interpretations:

contents.text: Marco is more annoyed by the noise than his sister is.
Marco is more annoyed by the noise than he is annoyed by his sister.

header.text: Illogical comparisons occur in a couple of ways:
1. The comparison compares two things that cannot be compared.

text.text: The average height of the buildings in New York is much higher than my town.

explanationText.text: You cannot compare the height of buildings to a town.

text.text: The average height of the buildings in New York is much higher than in my town.

header.text: 2. The comparison needs the word other or else to make sense.

text.text: I think blue is prettier than any color.

explanationText.text: Blue is a color. It cannot be prettier than itself.

text.text: I think blue is prettier than any other color.

header.text: 3. The comparison uses a superlative form instead of a comparative form, or vice versa.

text.text: Of the two of us, Alyssa is fastest.

explanationText.text: When comparing only two things, the comparative form should be used.

text.text: Of the two of us, Alyssa is faster.

contents.text: The pronouns who and whoever are subject pronouns. They act as subjects of sentences or clauses. The pronouns whom and whomever are object pronouns. They act as objects of action verbs or prepositions.
